_purpose: Human/AI-readable backup of what supabase/schema.sql + seed_categories.sql define. Not read by the app -- schema.sql is the source of truth. Regenerate this by hand if the schema changes materially.

database_purpose.summary: Powers two public directories on SpedCentral (special-education providers, and a products marketplace) plus the shared taxonomy both use for filtering/URLs.

domains.name: providers
domains.what_it_is: Directory of SPED specialists/companies (therapists, tutors, advocates, etc.) that parents search by state/city/category. Has an onboarding + moderation workflow (draft -> pending_review -> published/rejected/suspended).
domains.monetization: subscription_tier (free/basic/premium) + is_featured/featured_rank for paid placement; provider_leads captures the actual contact-form conversions.

domains.name: products
domains.what_it_is: Marketplace of assistive tech / sensory tools / printables. Two flavors via product_type: 'affiliate' (redirect to buy_url, no payment handling) and 'digital_download' (sold on-site, you take a cut, payout via Stripe Connect).
domains.monetization: product_orders records the money movement for digital_download sales only.

domains.name: shared reference data
domains.what_it_is: states, cities, languages, age_groups, environments, credentials, insurances -- lookup tables both domains filter/tag against, never joined to each other directly.

database_purpose.deliberately_not_in_db: Editorial content (guides, IEP help, glossary) -- lives as Markdown/MDX in Astro content collections instead, not a table. See bottom of schema.sql for why.

states.purpose: One row per US state, drives /texas/ style URLs.

cities.purpose: Cities within a state; self-referencing metro_id lets a suburb (Sugar Land) point at its metro hub (Houston).

languages.purpose: Languages a provider speaks / product is available in.

age_groups.purpose: Shared age-range taxonomy for both providers and products.

environments.purpose: Where a product is used (Home/School/etc.) -- products-domain only, orthogonal to product_categories.

credentials.purpose: Professional certifications a provider can hold (BCBA, OTR/L, etc.).

service_categories.purpose: Provider-domain taxonomy. Two-level: 7 top-level groups (nav/mega-menu) each with specific specialist types (the actual filter/URL slugs, e.g. /texas/houston/speech-language-pathologist/).
seeded_top_level_groups: medical-clinical-therapists (13 children, e.g. speech-language-pathologist, occupational-therapist, behavioral-therapist-aba)

providers.purpose: Core listing row -- one per specialist or company.

identity: parent_provider_id (fk self, nullable -- staff under a company)
ratings_denormalized: review_count (kept in sync by refresh_provider_rating() trigger)

providers.public_read_surface: public_providers view -- same columns minus submitted_by_email/admin_notes, filtered to status='published'

provider_hours.purpose: Weekly open hours, one row per day.

provider_photos.purpose: Gallery images (multiple per provider), separate from the single hero photo_url on providers.

provider_categories / provider_locations.purpose: Plain join tables (provider_id, <lookup>_id) linking providers to the reference tables above. No extra columns.
provider_categories / provider_locations.note: 6 tables, one per relationship, all cascade-delete with the provider.

provider_reviews.purpose: Star ratings + text, feeds the rating_avg/review_count on providers via trigger.

provider_leads.purpose: The actual revenue event: visitor -> provider contact-form submissions. Public insert-only, no public read.

product_categories.purpose: Products-domain taxonomy. 4 top-level groups by need (not product type), each with specific sub-categories.

creators.purpose: People/studios selling digital_download products only (not used for affiliate products). Payout destination for Stripe Connect.
creators.public_read_surface: public_creators view -- name/slug/bio/created_at only, omits email + stripe_connect_account_id
creators.note_no_image_field: No avatar/logo column exists yet for creators -- add one later (creators.avatar_url) if the creator marketplace needs a byline photo.

products.purpose: Core listing row -- one per product (affiliate or digital_download).

pricing: digital_file_url (digital_download only -- never public, served via signed URL post-payment)
media_IMAGE_FIELD: image_url (text -- single hero image, R2 URL)

product_photos.purpose: Gallery images (multiple per product), separate from the single hero image_url on products.

product_category_links / product_age_gro.purpose: Join tables linking products to product_categories / age_groups / environments.
product_category_links / product_age_gro.note: product_category_links allows a product in multiple categories at once (deliberate).

product_reviews.purpose: Star ratings + text, feeds rating_avg/review_count via trigger.

product_orders.purpose: digital_download purchase/money-movement records. Written server-side only via service_role after Stripe webhook confirms -- no public RLS policies at all.

image_fields_for_r2_planning.note: Every image column below is a plain `text` column storing a URL string -- schema.sql already comments photo_url/logo_url/image_url as 'Cloudflare R2 URL', so no schema change is needed to start using R2. The only decision left is WHAT to store in that text column.

columns.meaning: hero photo (individual) or logo (company, if logo_url unused)

image_fields_for_r2_planning.decision_STATUS: DECIDED 2026-07-27 -- going with key-only storage (option B). Do not revisit unless a real problem comes up.

decided_convention.what_gets_stored_in_the_db_column: Just the object key/path, e.g. providers/<provider_id>/hero.jpg -- NOT a full https:// URL.
decided_convention.how_the_full_url_is_built: At render time, prefix the stored key with one env var (PUBLIC_R2_BASE_URL, e.g. https://images.spedcentral.com/ or the R2.dev public URL) to get the real . Not implemented yet -- add a small helper (e.g. src/lib/images.ts: `r2Url(key)`) once the R2 bucket actually exists.
decided_convention.why: Provider/product UUID is already the natural, permanent key -- 'hero profile by key id' as you said. If the bucket, custom domain, or CDN ever changes, you update PUBLIC_R2_BASE_URL once instead of rewriting every photo_url/image_url row in the database.

image_fields_for_r2_planning.not_yet_wired: src/lib/images.ts currently resolves LOCAL build-time assets from src/assets/ by filename (for placeholder/seed data) -- unrelated to and will not be used once real photo_url/image_url columns hold R2 URLs. That helper can stay for any hand-picked editorial images but real listing photos will just be once R2 is wired.

row_level_security_summary.public_can_read: all reference/lookup tables, published providers/products (via base table policies + public_* views), published reviews
no_public_access_at_all: creators (public reads go through public_creators view instead)
row_level_security_summary.admin_actions: Approve/reject/suspend/delete and all edits to already-published listings happen through the service_role key from a protected server-side route -- bypasses RLS entirely. That key now lives in .env as SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY, unused until that route exists.

open_items_not_blocking_schema_run: No users/profiles table yet linking a future Clerk login to a providers row -- add when the provider-submission/login feature is actually built (tracked in project memory as deferred).
creators table has no avatar/photo column -- add later if needed, trivial ALTER TABLE, zero rows exist yet so no migration risk.

Decide full-URL vs key-only storage for image columns (see image_fields_for_r2_planning above) before the first real photo upload -- doesn't require a schema change either way, just a convention to commit to.
